settings.name_in_paper: Top-k eXtreme contextual bandit with arm hierarchy (realizable)
unmapped: Feedback: each chosen arm revealed with conditional probability >= c, c known
Known arm hierarchy tree T with routing functions g and beam width b; function class is (T,g,b)-constant (piecewise constant over context-dependent effective arms), giving Z = O(log A) effective arms
settings.definition_quote:
Given a hierarchy $\Tcal$ with routing function family $\{g_{h,i}(\cdot)\}$ and a beam-width $b$,
  a function $f(x,a)$ is $(\Tcal,g,b)$-constant if for every $ x \in \Xcal$
  \begin{align*}
    f(x, a) = f(x, a') \quad\text{for all}\quad a ,a' \in e_{h,i},
  \end{align*}
  for any node $e_{h,i}$ in $I_x \subset \cA_x$.  A class of functions $\Fcal$ is
  $(\Tcal,g,b)$-constant if each $f\in\Fcal$ is $(\Tcal,g,b)$-constant.

source.label: thm:topkregret
source.quote: Algorithm~\ref{alg:topk} under Assumptions~\ref{asum:realizability} and \ref{asum:feedback}, when run with parameters r = 1; N_l = 2^l; \gamma_l = ... has regret bound R(T) = \cO (k\sqrt{c^{-1}(A - k +1) T \log ( \frac{|\cF| T}{\delta} )}) with probability at least $1 - \delta$, for a finite function class $\cF$.

results.notes: Paper's A = K arms, k = m selected per round, |F| = N_exp. Regret is defined via f* means summed over rounds, stated w.p. 1-delta. Proof gives explicit constant 2308 c^{-1/2}(k+2)sqrt((A-k+1)T log(|F|T^3/delta)). Per-round computation is O~(A) given the regression oracle.
